record.original_question: For any configuration of N fixed electric charges in R^3 that has only finitely many equilibrium points, is the number of equilibrium points always at most (N - 1)^2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 (J. C. Maxwell). For any configuration of N fixed electric charges in R^3 having finitely many points of equilibrium, the number of the latter points is at most (N - 1)^2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \geq 2$ and let $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$ be nonzero real charges placed at distinct fixed points $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^3$. Consider the electrostatic (Coulomb) potential
$$ U(x) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{N} \frac{q_i}{\|x - x_i\|}, \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \{x_1, \dots, x_N\}, $$
and let $E(x) = -\nabla U(x)$ denote the corresponding electric field. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \{x_1, \dots, x_N\}$ is called an equilibrium point of the configuration if $E(x) = 0$, equivalently $\nabla U(x) = 0$.

Assume that the set of equilibrium points of the configuration is finite. Prove or disprove: the number of equilibrium points is at most $(N-1)^2$.
artifact.status_search_result: Maxwell's 1873 conjecture remains open in general. The first finite upper bound (far from $(N-1)^2$) was established in 2007 by Gabrielov, Novikov and Shapiro, who proved an upper bound of order $4N^2(3N)^{2N}$. Only partial results are known: the case $N=3$ with equal charges has been studied, and a related conjecture of Gabrielov–Novikov–Shapiro was recently disproved (2025 preprint on counting equilibria), but Maxwell's quadratic bound $(N-1)^2$ has been neither proved nor refuted.

status_evidence.title: Mystery of point charges
status_evidence.snippet: Maxwell conjectured that the number of points of equilibrium of the electrostatic field generated by N point charges in R^3 (assuming this number is finite) does not exceed (N-1)^2.
status_evidence.claim: Maxwell's conjecture is stated and remains unresolved; only an exponential-type upper bound is known.

status_evidence.title: Counting Equilibria of the Electrostatic Potential (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample to a conjecture of Gabrielov–Novikov–Shapiro; Maxwell's quadratic bound not known to be tight.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate, but Maxwell's $(N-1)^2$ bound is still open.

status_evidence.title: Maxwell's conjecture on three point charges with equal magnitudes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the special case N=3 with equal magnitudes.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases such as $N=3$ have been partially settled.
